title: Slot reuse lets a finished request's handle write bindings or writer state into the next request
claim: Acquire recycles a Dead slot (generation.Add then state.Store(Active)) without lifecycleMu, and alive() loads generation and state separately. A stale handle can therefore pass beginWrite while the slot is being reused, and BindObject*/UpdateWriter/AdoptBufferWriter/TruncateWriter/ResetWriter, which never re-check, publish the old request's objects and source IDs into the successor. The successor's source table then resolves those IDs, giving the wrong source or a false positive.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 REVIEW_STRESS=60s go test -run TestReviewStaleHandleBindAfterSlotReuse -count=1 -v ./internal/taint/store/ (harness: evidence/store-concurrency/zz_review_concurrency_test.go, unmodified code); deterministic consequence: evidence/store-concurrency/stale-handle-seam.txt

title: The same load-order gap lets Lookup build an Entry that mixes two owner generations
claim: Lookup checks generation and then state under RLock. If Acquire runs between the two loads, the successor's root with the same {rootID,rootGen} is copied and paired with the successor's OwnerID and the old OwnerGen. Entry.Handle and copySources currently reject this Entry.

title: A rebind racing a mutation claim undercounts value counters and can close the != 0 fast gates
claim: claimMutation(R1), run between putWindow's reserve on R2 and its release on R1, subtracts the key from values while R2 keeps it uncounted, so values can read 0 with live taint until Finish. This is latent: PublishBytesMutation has no production caller.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go test -race -run TestReviewSeamRebindMutationDrift -count=1 -v ./internal/taint/store/ (seam copy; diff in evidence)

title: No +checklocks: field annotations, so the CI checklocks run verifies nothing in the store
claim: None of the mutex-guarded fields (roots, rootFree, writers, writerCount, binding table, shard slots, overflow free list) are annotated, so go tool checklocks passes trivially and the +checklocksforce comments are inert.

title: Stale Finish has the same check-then-act shape, but no production path reaches it
claim: The generation check and the state CAS are not atomic together. In production each *Owner is finished at most once (request/owner.go:269-270 uses Swap(nil)), so a stale Finish cannot reach a reused slot.

title: Finish holds the process-wide overflowMu across its 512-root scan
claim: Other requests' blocking freeOverflow calls (rollbackRoot, PublishBytesMutation) wait for the whole scan. The wait is bounded and cannot deadlock, but it goes against the drop-rather-than-block policy.
